# Village Life
Village Life is my attempt to bring more detailed **micro-simulation** to Cities: Skylines II.
The idea is simple: citizens should behave more like actual people, with their own routines, needs, decisions, and problems, rather than just being numbers moving around the city.
One of my inspirations is the **Real Time mod for the original Cities: Skylines**. I'm not trying to recreate it, but I'm interested in the same general idea of making everyday citizen life more meaningful and believable.
## Micro and macro should agree
One of the main goals is to make the micro-simulation consistent with the game's macro-simulation.
Compared to the original Cities: Skylines, Cities: Skylines II has a much more detailed micro-simulation of individual citizens, but when you actually start following them around and observing their daily lives, you quickly realize how unrealistic their behavior can still be, despite all the underlying systems already in place.
Ideally, what happens to individual citizens should make sense when looking at the city as a whole, and vice versa.
## What does the mod currently do?
The mod already changes several aspects of everyday citizen behavior, including working, shopping, and leisure.
Citizens have more controlled shopping and leisure activities, with actual durations and more meaningful destination choices. Shopping involve physically visiting stores and completing purchases there instead of everything happening instantly.
Job seeking and switching have also been adjusted, particularly to make life in small settlements more practical.
Another important part is making citizen behavior more transparent. The mod adds **Life-Path messages** explaining what citizens are doing and why certain things succeed or fail. For example, you can see when someone cannot find a suitable job, when a shop doesn't have the requested resource, or what a citizen actually purchased.
There are also additional information panels showing citizen schedules, shopping and leisure activities, and the people visiting individual buildings.
## Where is this going?
The long-term goal is a more complete simulation of everyday life, where work, shopping, leisure, travel, sleeping, household finances, and other activities are connected rather than being mostly independent systems.
I also want to make it easier to understand what citizens are doing and why. Watching individual citizens should tell you something meaningful about how your city works.
This will be developed gradually, with new behaviors and improvements added over time.
## Development status
**Village Life is still very much in development.**
At this stage, I'm mainly experimenting with mechanics and trying to get the simulation working in a consistent and believable way.
**Optimization will come later.** For now, the focus is on functionality and behavior rather than performance, especially in larger cities. Expect bugs, unexpected behavior, and changes as the mod evolves.
## What about Small City Jobs?
Village Life is the continuation and expansion of my previous mod, **Small City Jobs**.
The original project started with improving employment behavior in small towns, but gradually expanded into shopping, leisure, and other parts of citizen life. At that point, the original name no longer really described what the mod was becoming.
**Small City Jobs will no longer be developed separately.** Future development will continue under Village Life.
The goal isn't necessarily to make the game easier or harder (but I do use it with hard mode). It's to make the simulation more interesting, understandable, and believable.
We'll see how far that can go!
For now, Village Life is primarily intended for village-sized settlements. There is no wiki for the mod, but you can find information about its features in the forum or by browsing the mod's changelog history.
